title: Tempest Flurry Guide — Four-hit Sequence, Final Strike, Shock and Bell Setup
summary: Tempest Flurry is a Quarterstaff attack that plays out as a four-use sequence: the first two uses hit once each, the third use lands three hits, and the fourth use is the Final Strike that launches a Shocking Bolt. This guide explains what happens on each use, when the sequence resets, how Attack Speed changes the feel, Quality, why some builds keep it at low gem level, and how to build a combo into Tempest Bell for bossing.
description: Tempest Flurry deep guide: the four-use attack sequence and Final Strike Shocking Bolt, multi-hit and AoE behaviour, Shock chance and magnitude, combo setup into Tempest Bell, support compatibility for speed and lightning, Weapon Set 2 shock duty, mapping and bossing rotations, troubleshooting (reset, bolt miss, low shock) and real community questions answered directly.

sections.title: Quick Answer: The Fourth Use Is the Final Strike
paragraphs: Tempest Flurry is not a uniform attack — it is a four-use sequence. Uses one and two hit once, use three hits three times, and use four is the Final Strike that fires a Shocking Bolt.
If you stop using the skill, the sequence resets back to the first use. So the payoff is always the fourth press; the earlier uses set it up.

sections.title: Requirements and Setup
paragraphs: Tempest Flurry needs a Quarterstaff and the attribute requirements of the gem. It is engraved from an Uncut Skill Gem, so the earliest you can use it is when a high-enough tier Uncut Skill Gem drops.
Because it is a sequence, it is usually the centre of a quarterstaff melee loop rather than a filler — you want to keep attacking so you actually reach the Final Strike.

keyValues.label: Weapon
notes: No quarterstaff means the sequence cannot start.

keyValues.label: Uncut gem tier
notes: Confirm the current client tier before publishing numbers.

sections.title: Four-use Attack Sequence
paragraphs: Each press of Tempest Flurry advances the sequence. The first two uses are single hits, the third use is a three-hit flurry, and the fourth use is the Final Strike that launches a Shocking Bolt. Reaching the fourth use is what makes the skill worth using.

sections.title: Hit Behaviour: Multi-hit, Bolt and AoE
paragraphs: The third use's three hits can each apply on-hit effects, which is why builds that scale per-hit damage like it. The fourth use's Shocking Bolt is a projectile-like lightning effect that can shock the target it strikes.
Area modifiers change how wide the strikes feel, but the sequence structure (1 / 1 / 3 / Final) stays the same regardless of Attack Speed.
bullets: 3rd use: three separate hits (per-hit scaling applies).
4th use: Final Strike fires a Shocking Bolt.
AoE modifiers widen the strikes but not the sequence.

sections.title: Shock Chance and Magnitude
paragraphs: The Shocking Bolt from the Final Strike can Shock, and the skill's shock magnitude scales with its own modifiers. Shock is what makes Tempest Flurry valuable for bossing even on builds that only press it to apply Shock.
Shock chance is not automatic at 100% — supports and gear that raise shock chance / magnitude directly improve the bossing payoff. Low shock is almost always a gear or support gap, not a bug.

steps.label: Final Strike
steps.action: Reach the 4th use inside the Bell window
steps.result: The Shocking Bolt and Final Strike are amplified by the Bell.

sections.title: Support Compatibility
paragraphs: Attack Speed supports help you reach the Final Strike faster but do not skip uses. Lightning and added-lightning supports scale the Shocking Bolt and shock magnitude. Final Strike supports that boost the last hit are the biggest single-target winners.

keyValues.label: Attack Speed
notes: Faster cadence to the Final Strike, no skipped uses.

keyValues.label: Added Lightning / Lightning Infusion
notes: Scales the Shocking Bolt and shock magnitude.

sections.title: Weapon Set 2 Shock Duty
paragraphs: Some builds keep Tempest Flurry on Weapon Set 2 purely as a Shock applicator, using the quarterstaff only to land the Final Strike Shocking Bolt on a boss before swapping back to the main set.
Because the sequence resets on stop, a Weapon Set 2 shock build usually commits to reaching the fourth use quickly rather than weaving it into a longer rotation.

sections.title: Where It Is Used
paragraphs: Leveling quarterstaff builds use Tempest Flurry as a smooth primary attack. Whirling Assault martial artists pair it with Whirling Assault for movement plus burst, and some unique-focused routes (Duality / Finality style) keep the gem at low level purely to apply Shock cheaply.
In every case the build values either the Final Strike burst or the Shock application, depending on whether it is a damage or support role.
bullets: Whirling martial artist: pairs with Whirling Assault.
Unique Shock routes: low gem level for cheap Shock.

steps.label: Sequence keeps resetting

steps.label: Bolt does not hit
steps.action: Target moved out of the Final Strike line

steps.label: Shock too low
steps.result: Add lightning supports and shock-chance modifiers.

sections.title: Community Evidence
paragraphs: Community discussion clusters on low gem level (cheap Shock), attack-speed feel, and whether to press all four uses. Client testing confirms the sequence is fixed at 1 / 1 / 3 / Final and that Attack Speed only changes cadence, not the hit count.
The main misconception is that faster Attack Speed skips uses — it does not; it just reaches the Final Strike sooner.
